solution:
Write the function with negative indices so the power rule applies throughout:
\(y = 2x^5 - 4x^3 - 2x^{-2} - 9\)
Differentiating once,
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = 10x^4 - 12x^2 + 4x^{-3}\)
Differentiating again,
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 40x^3 - 24x - 12x^{-4}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 40x^3 - 24x - \frac{12}{x^4}\)

\(y = e^{2x} \cdot \tan x\). Use the product rule.
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2e^{2x}\tan x + e^{2x}\sec^2 x = e^{2x}\left(2\tan x + \sec^2 x\right)\)
Differentiate again, using the product rule once more and \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sec^2 x) = 2\sec^2 x \tan x\):
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2e^{2x}\left(2\tan x + \sec^2 x\right) + e^{2x}\left(2\sec^2 x + 2\sec^2 x \tan x\right)\)
\(= e^{2x}\left(4\tan x + 2\sec^2 x + 2\sec^2 x + 2\sec^2 x \tan x\right)\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2e^{2x}\left(2\tan x + 2\sec^2 x + \sec^2 x \tan x\right)\)

\(y = e^{4x} \cdot \cos 5x\). Use the product rule.
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = 4e^{4x}\cos 5x + e^{4x}(-5\sin 5x) = e^{4x}\left(4\cos 5x - 5\sin 5x\right)\)
Differentiate again:
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 4e^{4x}\left(4\cos 5x - 5\sin 5x\right) + e^{4x}\left(-20\sin 5x - 25\cos 5x\right)\)
\(= e^{4x}\left(16\cos 5x - 20\sin 5x - 20\sin 5x - 25\cos 5x\right)\)
\(= e^{4x}\left(-9\cos 5x - 40\sin 5x\right)\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -e^{4x}\left(9\cos 5x + 40\sin 5x\right)\)

\(y = x^3 \log x\). Use the product rule.
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 \log x + x^3 \cdot \frac{1}{x} = 3x^2 \log x + x^2\)
Differentiate again:
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6x \log x + 3x^2 \cdot \frac{1}{x} + 2x = 6x \log x + 3x + 2x\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6x \log x + 5x = x\left(6 \log x + 5\right)\)

\(y = \log (\log x)\). By the chain rule,
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{\log x} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\log x) = \frac{1}{x \log x}\)
Write \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \left(x \log x\right)^{-1}\) and differentiate again, noting \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(x \log x\right) = \log x + 1\):
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\left(x \log x\right)^{-2} \cdot \left(\log x + 1\right)\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{1 + \log x}{x^2 \left(\log x\right)^2}\)

\(y = x^x\). The base and the index both vary, so use logarithmic differentiation.
Taking logarithms, \(\log y = x \log x\).
Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\):
\(\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 \cdot \log x + x \cdot \frac{1}{x} = \log x + 1\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx} = y\left(1 + \log x\right) = x^x \left(1 + \log x\right)\)
Now differentiate once more, by the product rule:
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{d}{dx}\left(x^x\right)\left(1 + \log x\right) + x^x \cdot \frac{1}{x}\)
\(= x^x\left(1 + \log x\right)\left(1 + \log x\right) + x^x \cdot \frac{1}{x}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = x^x\left[\left(1 + \log x\right)^2 + \frac{1}{x}\right]\)

\(x = a(\theta - \sin \theta)\), \(y = a(1 - \cos \theta)\).
Differentiate each with respect to \(\theta\):
\(\frac{dx}{d\theta} = a(1 - \cos \theta)\), \(\frac{dy}{d\theta} = a \sin \theta\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta} = \frac{a \sin \theta}{a(1 - \cos \theta)} = \frac{2 \sin \frac{\theta}{2}\cos \frac{\theta}{2}}{2 \sin^2 \frac{\theta}{2}} = \cot \frac{\theta}{2}\)
For the second derivative do NOT divide \(\frac{d^2y}{d\theta^2}\) by \(\frac{d^2x}{d\theta^2}\). Since \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) is a function of \(\theta\), use
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{d}{d\theta}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) \cdot \frac{d\theta}{dx}\)
\(\frac{d}{d\theta}\left(\cot \frac{\theta}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosec}^2 \frac{\theta}{2}\) and \(\frac{d\theta}{dx} = \frac{1}{a(1 - \cos \theta)} = \frac{1}{2a \sin^2 \frac{\theta}{2}}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosec}^2 \frac{\theta}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2a \sin^2 \frac{\theta}{2}} = -\frac{1}{4a \sin^4 \frac{\theta}{2}}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{1}{4a}\operatorname{cosec}^4 \frac{\theta}{2}\)

\(x = 2at^2\), \(y = 4at\).
\(\frac{dx}{dt} = 4at\), \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 4a\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{4a}{4at} = \frac{1}{t}\)
Since \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) is a function of \(t\), differentiate it with respect to \(t\) and multiply by \(\frac{dt}{dx}\):
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right) \cdot \frac{dt}{dx} = \left(-\frac{1}{t^2}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{4at}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{1}{4at^3}\)

\(x = \sin \theta\), \(y = \sin^3 \theta\).
\(\frac{dx}{d\theta} = \cos \theta\), \(\frac{dy}{d\theta} = 3 \sin^2 \theta \cos \theta\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3 \sin^2 \theta \cos \theta}{\cos \theta} = 3 \sin^2 \theta\)
Now differentiate with respect to \(\theta\) and multiply by \(\frac{d\theta}{dx}\):
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{d}{d\theta}\left(3 \sin^2 \theta\right) \cdot \frac{d\theta}{dx} = 6 \sin \theta \cos \theta \cdot \frac{1}{\cos \theta} = 6 \sin \theta\)
At \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\sin \theta = 1\).
\(\therefore \left(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)_{\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}} = 6\)
As a check, \(y = \sin^3\theta = x^3\), so \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6x = 6 \sin \theta\), which agrees.

\(x = a \cos \theta\), \(y = b \sin \theta\).
\(\frac{dx}{d\theta} = -a \sin \theta\), \(\frac{dy}{d\theta} = b \cos \theta\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{b \cos \theta}{-a \sin \theta} = -\frac{b}{a}\cot \theta\)
Differentiate with respect to \(\theta\) and multiply by \(\frac{d\theta}{dx}\):
\(\frac{d}{d\theta}\left(-\frac{b}{a}\cot \theta\right) = \frac{b}{a}\operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta\) and \(\frac{d\theta}{dx} = \frac{1}{-a \sin \theta}\)
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{b}{a}\operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{a \sin \theta}\right) = -\frac{b}{a^2}\operatorname{cosec}^3 \theta\)
At \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\frac{\pi}{4} = \sqrt{2}\), so \(\operatorname{cosec}^3\frac{\pi}{4} = 2\sqrt{2}\).
\(\therefore \left(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)_{\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}} = -\frac{2\sqrt{2}\,b}{a^2}\)

\(x = at^2\), \(y = 2at\).
\(\frac{dx}{dt} = 2at\), \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 2a\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2a}{2at} = \frac{1}{t}\)
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right)\cdot\frac{dt}{dx} = \left(-\frac{1}{t^2}\right)\cdot\frac{1}{2at} = -\frac{1}{2at^3}\)
Now \(xy = at^2 \cdot 2at = 2a^2 t^3\), so
\(xy\,\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2a^2 t^3 \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2at^3}\right) = -a\)
\(\therefore xy\,\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + a = -a + a = 0\), as required.

\(y = e^{m \tan^{-1} x}\).
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = e^{m \tan^{-1} x} \cdot \frac{m}{1 + x^2} = \frac{m\,y}{1 + x^2}\)
Clear the denominator so a second differentiation stays simple:
\(\left(1 + x^2\right)\frac{dy}{dx} = m\,y\)
Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\), using the product rule on the left:
\(2x\,\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(1 + x^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = m\,\frac{dy}{dx}\)
\(\left(1 + x^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 2x\,\frac{dy}{dx} - m\,\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\)
\(\therefore \left(1 + x^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + (2x - m)\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\), as required.

\(x = \cos t\), \(y = e^{mt}\).
\(\frac{dx}{dt} = -\sin t\), \(\frac{dy}{dt} = m e^{mt}\)
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{m e^{mt}}{-\sin t} = -\frac{m e^{mt}}{\sin t}\)
For the second derivative, differentiate with respect to \(t\) and multiply by \(\frac{dt}{dx} = -\frac{1}{\sin t}\):
\(\frac{d}{dt}\left(-\frac{m e^{mt}}{\sin t}\right) = -m \cdot \frac{m e^{mt}\sin t - e^{mt}\cos t}{\sin^2 t} = -\frac{m e^{mt}\left(m \sin t - \cos t\right)}{\sin^2 t}\)
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{m e^{mt}\left(m \sin t - \cos t\right)}{\sin^2 t}\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{\sin t}\right) = \frac{m e^{mt}\left(m \sin t - \cos t\right)}{\sin^3 t}\)
Now substitute into the left side, using \(x = \cos t\) so that \(1 - x^2 = \sin^2 t\), and \(y = e^{mt}\):
\(\left(1 - x^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} - x\,\frac{dy}{dx} - m^2 y\)
\(= \sin^2 t \cdot \frac{m e^{mt}\left(m \sin t - \cos t\right)}{\sin^3 t} - \cos t \cdot \left(-\frac{m e^{mt}}{\sin t}\right) - m^2 e^{mt}\)
\(= \frac{m e^{mt}\left(m \sin t - \cos t\right)}{\sin t} + \frac{m e^{mt}\cos t}{\sin t} - m^2 e^{mt}\)
\(= \frac{m^2 e^{mt}\sin t - m e^{mt}\cos t + m e^{mt}\cos t}{\sin t} - m^2 e^{mt}\)
\(= m^2 e^{mt} - m^2 e^{mt} = 0\)
\(\therefore \left(1 - x^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} - x\,\frac{dy}{dx} - m^2 y = 0\), as required.

\(y = x + \tan x\).
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 + \sec^2 x\)
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2 \sec x \cdot \sec x \tan x = 2 \sec^2 x \tan x\)
Multiply by \(\cos^2 x\), noting \(\sec^2 x \cos^2 x = 1\):
\(\cos^2 x \cdot \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2 \cos^2 x \sec^2 x \tan x = 2 \tan x\)
From the given relation, \(\tan x = y - x\), so
\(\cos^2 x \cdot \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2(y - x) = 2y - 2x\)
\(\therefore \cos^2 x \cdot \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 2y + 2x = 2y - 2x - 2y + 2x = 0\), as required.

\(y = e^{ax}\sin (bx)\).
\(y_1 = a e^{ax}\sin bx + b e^{ax}\cos bx = a\,y + b e^{ax}\cos bx\)
Hence \(b e^{ax}\cos bx = y_1 - a\,y\). Differentiate \(y_1\) once more:
\(y_2 = a\,y_1 + b\left(a e^{ax}\cos bx - b e^{ax}\sin bx\right)\)
\(= a\,y_1 + a\left(b e^{ax}\cos bx\right) - b^2 e^{ax}\sin bx\)
Substitute \(b e^{ax}\cos bx = y_1 - a\,y\) and \(e^{ax}\sin bx = y\):
\(y_2 = a\,y_1 + a\left(y_1 - a\,y\right) - b^2 y = 2a\,y_1 - a^2 y - b^2 y\)
\(\therefore y_2 - 2a\,y_1 + \left(a^2 + b^2\right)y = 0\), as required.

\(\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{7x^3 - 5y^3}{7x^3 + 5y^3}\right) = m\), where \(m\) is a constant.
Taking secant of both sides,
\(\frac{7x^3 - 5y^3}{7x^3 + 5y^3} = \sec m\)
Since \(m\) is a constant, \(\sec m\) is a constant; call it \(k\). Then
\(7x^3 - 5y^3 = k\left(7x^3 + 5y^3\right)\)
\(7x^3(1 - k) = 5y^3(1 + k)\)
\(y^3 = \frac{7(1 - k)}{5(1 + k)}\,x^3\)
The coefficient on the right is a constant, so taking cube roots gives
\(y = c\,x\), where \(c = \left[\frac{7(1 - k)}{5(1 + k)}\right]^{1/3}\) is a constant.
Thus \(y\) is a linear function of \(x\). Differentiating twice,
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = c\) and \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\), as required.

\(2y = \sqrt{x + 1} + \sqrt{x - 1}\).
Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2y_1 = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x - 1}} = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{x - 1} + \sqrt{x + 1}}{\sqrt{x + 1}\,\sqrt{x - 1}}\)
The numerator is exactly \(2y\), and \(\sqrt{x + 1}\,\sqrt{x - 1} = \sqrt{x^2 - 1}\), so
\(2y_1 = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2y}{\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}\)
\(2y_1 \sqrt{x^2 - 1} = y\)
Square both sides to remove the radical:
\(4y_1^2\left(x^2 - 1\right) = y^2\)
Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\):
\(4\left[2y_1 y_2\left(x^2 - 1\right) + y_1^2 \cdot 2x\right] = 2y\,y_1\)
\(8y_1 y_2\left(x^2 - 1\right) + 8x\,y_1^2 = 2y\,y_1\)
Divide throughout by \(2y_1\) (which is not identically zero):
\(4\left(x^2 - 1\right)y_2 + 4x\,y_1 = y\)
\(\therefore 4\left(x^2 - 1\right)y_2 + 4x\,y_1 - y = 0\), as required.

\(y = \log \left(x + \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\right)^m\). The argument of the logarithm is raised to \(m\), so
\(y = m \log \left(x + \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\right)\)
Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = m \cdot \frac{1}{x + \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}} \cdot \left(1 + \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}}\right)\)
\(= m \cdot \frac{1}{x + \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{x^2 + a^2} + x}{\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}}\)
The bracket \(x + \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\) cancels, leaving
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{m}{\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}}\)
Write this as \(\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\,\frac{dy}{dx} = m\) and differentiate again, using the product rule:
\(\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}}\cdot\frac{dy}{dx} + \sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\,\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\)
Multiply throughout by \(\sqrt{x^2 + a^2}\):
\(x\,\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(x^2 + a^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\)
\(\therefore \left(x^2 + a^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\,\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\), as required.

\(y = \sin \left(m \cos^{-1} x\right)\).
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \cos \left(m \cos^{-1} x\right) \cdot m \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\right) = \frac{-m \cos \left(m \cos^{-1} x\right)}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\)
Hence \(\sqrt{1 - x^2}\,\frac{dy}{dx} = -m \cos \left(m \cos^{-1} x\right)\).
Square both sides, and use \(\cos^2 \left(m \cos^{-1} x\right) = 1 - \sin^2 \left(m \cos^{-1} x\right) = 1 - y^2\):
\(\left(1 - x^2\right)\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = m^2 \left(1 - y^2\right)\)
Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\):
\(-2x\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + \left(1 - x^2\right)\cdot 2\,\frac{dy}{dx}\cdot\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -2m^2 y\,\frac{dy}{dx}\)
Divide throughout by \(2\,\frac{dy}{dx}\) (which is not identically zero):
\(-x\,\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(1 - x^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -m^2 y\)
\(\therefore \left(1 - x^2\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} - x\,\frac{dy}{dx} + m^2 y = 0\), as required.

\(y = \log (\log 2x)\).
\(y_1 = \frac{1}{\log 2x}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}\left(\log 2x\right) = \frac{1}{\log 2x}\cdot\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{x \log 2x}\)
Rearranging, \(x\,\left(\log 2x\right) y_1 = 1\). Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\), using the product rule and \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(x \log 2x\right) = \log 2x + 1\):
\(\left(\log 2x + 1\right)y_1 + x\left(\log 2x\right) y_2 = 0\)
From \(y_1 = \frac{1}{x \log 2x}\) we get \(x \log 2x = \frac{1}{y_1}\) and \(\log 2x = \frac{1}{x\,y_1}\). Substituting both:
\(\left(\frac{1}{x\,y_1} + 1\right)y_1 + \frac{1}{y_1}\,y_2 = 0\)
Multiply throughout by \(y_1\):
\(\left(\frac{1}{x\,y_1} + 1\right)y_1^2 + y_2 = 0\)
\(\frac{y_1}{x} + y_1^2 + y_2 = 0\)
Multiply throughout by \(x\):
\(y_1 + x\,y_1^2 + x\,y_2 = 0\)
\(\therefore x\,y_2 + y_1\left(1 + x\,y_1\right) = 0\), as required.

\(x^2 + 6xy + y^2 = 10\). Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\), treating \(y\) as a function of \(x\):
\(2x + 6y + 6x\,\frac{dy}{dx} + 2y\,\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\)
Divide by \(2\) and collect:
\(x + 3y + \left(3x + y\right)\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\)
\(\therefore \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x + 3y}{3x + y}\)
Differentiate \(x + 3y + \left(3x + y\right)\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) once more with respect to \(x\):
\(1 + 3\,\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(3 + \frac{dy}{dx}\right)\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(3x + y\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\)
\(\left(3x + y\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\left[1 + 6\,\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]\)
Substitute \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{x + 3y}{3x + y}\) and take the common denominator \(\left(3x + y\right)^2\):
\(1 + 6\,\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \frac{\left(3x + y\right)^2 - 6\left(x + 3y\right)\left(3x + y\right) + \left(x + 3y\right)^2}{\left(3x + y\right)^2}\)
Expanding the numerator:
\(\left(9x^2 + 6xy + y^2\right) - 6\left(3x^2 + 10xy + 3y^2\right) + \left(x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2\right) = -8x^2 - 48xy - 8y^2\)
\(= -8\left(x^2 + 6xy + y^2\right) = -8(10) = -80\), using the given equation.
Therefore
\(\left(3x + y\right)\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\left(\frac{-80}{\left(3x + y\right)^2}\right) = \frac{80}{\left(3x + y\right)^2}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{80}{\left(3x + y\right)^3}\), as required.

\(x = a \sin t - b \cos t\), \(y = a \cos t + b \sin t\).
Differentiate each with respect to \(t\):
\(\frac{dx}{dt} = a \cos t + b \sin t = y\)
\(\frac{dy}{dt} = -a \sin t + b \cos t = -\left(a \sin t - b \cos t\right) = -x\)
So the parametric derivatives are simply \(y\) and \(-x\), and
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = -\frac{x}{y}\)
For the second derivative, differentiate \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) with respect to \(t\) and multiply by \(\frac{dt}{dx} = \frac{1}{y}\). By the quotient rule,
\(\frac{d}{dt}\left(-\frac{x}{y}\right) = -\frac{\frac{dx}{dt}\cdot y - x \cdot \frac{dy}{dt}}{y^2} = -\frac{y \cdot y - x(-x)}{y^2} = -\frac{x^2 + y^2}{y^2}\)
Hence
\(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{x^2 + y^2}{y^2}\cdot\frac{1}{y}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{x^2 + y^2}{y^3}\), as required.

\(y = (ax + b)^m\). Differentiate repeatedly, each time bringing down the current index and multiplying by \(a\) from the chain rule.
\(y_1 = m\,a\,(ax + b)^{m-1}\)
\(y_2 = m(m - 1)\,a^2\,(ax + b)^{m-2}\)
\(y_3 = m(m - 1)(m - 2)\,a^3\,(ax + b)^{m-3}\)
The pattern is clear: after \(n\) differentiations there are \(n\) descending factors starting at \(m\), the last being \(m - n + 1\), and a factor \(a^n\).
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = m(m - 1)(m - 2)\cdots(m - n + 1)\,a^n\,(ax + b)^{m-n}\)
When \(m\) is a positive integer with \(m \geq n\) this may be written as
\(\frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = \frac{m!}{(m - n)!}\,a^n\,(ax + b)^{m-n}\)

\(y = \frac{1}{x} = x^{-1}\).
\(y_1 = -x^{-2}\)
\(y_2 = (-1)(-2)\,x^{-3} = 2\,x^{-3}\)
\(y_3 = (-1)(-2)(-3)\,x^{-4} = -6\,x^{-4}\)
Each differentiation contributes one more negative factor, so the sign alternates as \((-1)^n\), and the magnitudes \(1, 2, 6, 24, \ldots\) are \(n!\). The index of \(x\) after \(n\) steps is \(-(n + 1)\).
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = \frac{(-1)^n\, n!}{x^{n+1}}\)

\(y = e^{ax + b}\). Each differentiation reproduces the function and brings out a factor \(a\) by the chain rule.
\(y_1 = a\,e^{ax + b}\)
\(y_2 = a^2\,e^{ax + b}\)
\(y_3 = a^3\,e^{ax + b}\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = a^n\,e^{ax + b}\)

\(y = a^{px + q}\). Recall \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(a^u\right) = a^u \log a \cdot \frac{du}{dx}\). Here \(u = px + q\), so \(\frac{du}{dx} = p\).
\(y_1 = a^{px + q}\,\log a \cdot p = p\,(\log a)\,a^{px + q}\)
\(y_2 = p^2\,(\log a)^2\,a^{px + q}\)
\(y_3 = p^3\,(\log a)^3\,a^{px + q}\)
Each differentiation contributes one further factor \(p \log a\).
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = p^n\,(\log a)^n\,a^{px + q}\)

\(y = \log (ax + b)\). The first derivative removes the logarithm; after that it is a power of \((ax + b)\).
\(y_1 = \frac{a}{ax + b} = a\,(ax + b)^{-1}\)
\(y_2 = a \cdot (-1)(ax + b)^{-2}\cdot a = -\frac{a^2}{(ax + b)^2}\)
\(y_3 = \frac{2a^3}{(ax + b)^3}\)
So from \(y_1\) onward the sign alternates, starting positive at \(n = 1\), which is \((-1)^{n-1}\); the numerical factor runs \(1, 1, 2, 6, \ldots = (n - 1)!\); and each step contributes another \(a\), giving \(a^n\).
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = \frac{(-1)^{n-1}\,(n - 1)!\;a^n}{(ax + b)^n}\)

\(y = \cos x\). Use the fact that differentiating a cosine advances its angle by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), since \(-\sin x = \cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).
\(y_1 = -\sin x = \cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)
\(y_2 = \cos\left(x + \frac{2\pi}{2}\right) = -\cos x\)
\(y_3 = \cos\left(x + \frac{3\pi}{2}\right) = \sin x\)
\(y_4 = \cos\left(x + \frac{4\pi}{2}\right) = \cos x\)
Each differentiation adds \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) to the angle, and the values repeat with period \(4\).
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = \cos\left(x + \frac{n\pi}{2}\right)\)

\(y = \sin (ax + b)\). Differentiating a sine advances its angle by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), since \(\cos u = \sin\left(u + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\); the chain rule contributes a factor \(a\) each time.
\(y_1 = a \cos (ax + b) = a \sin\left(ax + b + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)
\(y_2 = a^2 \sin\left(ax + b + \frac{2\pi}{2}\right)\)
\(y_3 = a^3 \sin\left(ax + b + \frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = a^n \sin\left(ax + b + \frac{n\pi}{2}\right)\)

\(y = \cos (3 - 2x)\). This is \(\cos (ax + b)\) with \(a = -2\) and \(b = 3\). Differentiating a cosine advances its angle by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), and the chain rule contributes \(a = -2\) each time.
\(y_1 = -(-2)\sin (3 - 2x) = 2 \sin (3 - 2x)\), and in the standard form \(y_1 = (-2)\cos\left(3 - 2x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = (-2)\left(-\sin (3 - 2x)\right) = 2 \sin (3 - 2x)\), which agrees.
\(y_2 = (-2)^2 \cos\left(3 - 2x + \frac{2\pi}{2}\right) = -4 \cos (3 - 2x)\)
\(y_3 = (-2)^3 \cos\left(3 - 2x + \frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = (-2)^n \cos\left(3 - 2x + \frac{n\pi}{2}\right)\)

\(y = \log (2x + 3)\). This is \(\log (ax + b)\) with \(a = 2\), \(b = 3\).
\(y_1 = \frac{2}{2x + 3} = 2\,(2x + 3)^{-1}\)
\(y_2 = 2 \cdot (-1)(2x + 3)^{-2}\cdot 2 = -\frac{2^2}{(2x + 3)^2}\)
\(y_3 = \frac{2 \cdot 2^3}{(2x + 3)^3} = \frac{2!\;2^3}{(2x + 3)^3}\)
The sign alternates starting positive at \(n = 1\), giving \((-1)^{n-1}\); the numerical factor is \((n - 1)!\); and each differentiation contributes another \(2\), giving \(2^n\).
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = \frac{(-1)^{n-1}\,(n - 1)!\;2^n}{(2x + 3)^n}\)

\(y = \frac{1}{3x - 5} = (3x - 5)^{-1}\). Each differentiation lowers the index by one and contributes a factor \(3\) from the chain rule.
\(y_1 = -1 \cdot (3x - 5)^{-2}\cdot 3 = -\frac{3}{(3x - 5)^2}\)
\(y_2 = (-1)(-2)\,(3x - 5)^{-3}\cdot 3^2 = \frac{2!\;3^2}{(3x - 5)^3}\)
\(y_3 = (-1)(-2)(-3)\,(3x - 5)^{-4}\cdot 3^3 = -\frac{3!\;3^3}{(3x - 5)^4}\)
The sign is \((-1)^n\), the numerical factor is \(n!\), the power of \(3\) is \(3^n\), and the index of \((3x - 5)\) is \(-(n + 1)\).
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = \frac{(-1)^n\, n!\;3^n}{(3x - 5)^{n+1}}\)

\(y = e^{ax}\cos (bx + c)\).
\(y_1 = a e^{ax}\cos (bx + c) - b e^{ax}\sin (bx + c) = e^{ax}\left[a \cos (bx + c) - b \sin (bx + c)\right]\)
The bracket is a linear combination of a cosine and a sine of the same angle, so express it as a single cosine. Put
\(a = r \cos \alpha\), \(b = r \sin \alpha\), so that \(r = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\alpha = \tan^{-1}\frac{b}{a}\).
Then
\(a \cos (bx + c) - b \sin (bx + c) = r\left[\cos \alpha \cos (bx + c) - \sin \alpha \sin (bx + c)\right] = r \cos (bx + c + \alpha)\)
Hence
\(y_1 = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\;e^{ax}\cos (bx + c + \alpha)\)
The effect of one differentiation is therefore to multiply by \(\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and to advance the angle by \(\alpha\). The result has exactly the same form as \(y\), with \(c\) replaced by \(c + \alpha\), so the same step applies again:
\(y_2 = \left(\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\right)^2 e^{ax}\cos (bx + c + 2\alpha) = \left(a^2 + b^2\right)e^{ax}\cos (bx + c + 2\alpha)\)
\(y_3 = \left(a^2 + b^2\right)^{3/2} e^{ax}\cos (bx + c + 3\alpha)\)
Repeating \(n\) times:
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = \left(a^2 + b^2\right)^{n/2} e^{ax}\cos \left(bx + c + n\alpha\right)\), where \(\alpha = \tan^{-1}\frac{b}{a}\)

\(y = e^{8x}\cos (6x + 7)\). This is \(e^{ax}\cos (bx + c)\) with \(a = 8\), \(b = 6\), \(c = 7\).
\(y_1 = 8 e^{8x}\cos (6x + 7) - 6 e^{8x}\sin (6x + 7) = e^{8x}\left[8 \cos (6x + 7) - 6 \sin (6x + 7)\right]\)
Combine the bracket into a single cosine by putting \(8 = r \cos \alpha\), \(6 = r \sin \alpha\). Then
\(r = \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{64 + 36} = \sqrt{100} = 10\) and \(\alpha = \tan^{-1}\frac{6}{8} = \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4}\)
so that
\(8 \cos (6x + 7) - 6 \sin (6x + 7) = 10\left[\cos \alpha \cos (6x + 7) - \sin \alpha \sin (6x + 7)\right] = 10 \cos (6x + 7 + \alpha)\)
Hence
\(y_1 = 10\,e^{8x}\cos (6x + 7 + \alpha)\)
One differentiation multiplies by \(10\) and advances the angle by \(\alpha\), and the result has the same form as \(y\), so the step repeats:
\(y_2 = 10^2\,e^{8x}\cos (6x + 7 + 2\alpha)\)
\(y_3 = 10^3\,e^{8x}\cos (6x + 7 + 3\alpha)\)
\(\therefore \frac{d^ny}{dx^n} = 10^n\,e^{8x}\cos \left(6x + 7 + n\,\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{4}\right)\)
